campaign: safe-c33: repair the shared ASN.1 template walk's inline-boolean slot access, and re-adjudicate the last two BLOCKED rows (v2i_idp, v2i_aaidp)
subphase: B57 reproduces B55-F1, fixes it structurally in the shared template walk, proves the correction with a load-bearing control, and re-adjudicates the two X509 rows B55 left BLOCKED. Reproduction first: a safe caller reaching ISSUING_DIST_POINT or OSSL_AA_DIST_POINT through X509V3_EXT_nconf_nid aborted in the generic free/encode/print walk with `misaligned pointer dereference: address must be a multiple of 0x8` (free: src/asn1/fre.rs:218; encode: src/asn1/i2d.rs:234; print: src/asn1/tasn_prn.rs:218). Root cause: a template field is reached as `base + offset` and the walk dereferenced it as an eight-byte `ASN1_VALUE **`, but an inline ASN1_BOOLEAN is a four-byte `int` at a four-byte-aligned offset. The repair adds one width-aware inline-boolean abstraction in src/asn1/utl.rs and uses it at every generic read/write site; no ABI, layout or exported symbol changed. Proving the fix surfaced a second independent defect in the same row: OSSL_AA_DIST_POINT_TT hardcoded template offsets 16/20/24/28 while the authority's `offsetof` gives 20/24/28/32 (the struct has `dp_reasons` at 16), so the boolean fields were encoded from the wrong slots; the offsets are now derived with `core::mem::offset_of!`. Both rows are SAFETY_DISCHARGED, site-scoped. Nothing is applied; CAMPAIGN-STATUS.json / state.json are untouched, and nothing was committed or pushed.

authority.contract: crypto/x509/v3_crld.c:344-351 (ISSUING_DIST_POINT) and :554-560 (OSSL_AA_DIST_POINT) build their ASN1_SEQUENCE with ASN1_EXP_OPT/ASN1_IMP_OPT, whose template offset is `offsetof(stname, field)`. `ASN1_BOOLEAN` is `int` (four bytes; include/openssl/asn1.h), and include/openssl/x509v3.h:2004-2012 places `dp_reasons` at offset 16, so OSSL_AA_DIST_POINT's booleans are at offsets 20/24/28/32.
authority.observed_authority_read: ossl_asn1_item_embed_free and asn1_item_embed_i2d read `*pval` as `ASN1_VALUE *` before the item-type dispatch. For an inline boolean at a four-byte-aligned offset that C read is an unaligned, over-wide load (and at the last field four bytes past the allocation). The crate must not reproduce it: Rust makes the misaligned read UB, and debug builds abort with `misaligned pointer dereference`.
authority.deviation: The candidate never forms a pointer-typed access for an inline ASN1_BOOLEAN: the free, encode, decode and print walks skip the pointer-shaped presence read for `is_inline_boolean(it)` and read/write the field with `ptr::read_unaligned`/`ptr::write_unaligned` at `c_int` width. Wire encoding and set/clear semantics are unchanged and are asserted byte-for-byte. Recorded per AGENTS.md section 17.

mechanism.state: OWNERSHIP_RECONSTRUCTED (mechanism-wide); this receipt repairs the inline-boolean slot access and is SITE-SCOPED for the two discharged rows
mechanism.root_cause: `get_field_ptr`/`get_const_field_ptr` return `base + tt.offset` cast to `*mut *mut c_void`. The generic walks then read `*pval` as an eight-byte pointer to decide whether the field is present. An inline ASN1_BOOLEAN (ASN1_FBOOLEAN_it / ASN1_TBOOLEAN_it) stores a four-byte `int` in the slot, and the dist-point fields sit at 4-byte-aligned offsets, so that read is simultaneously over-wide and misaligned. Rust's debug-mode check turns it into a non-unwinding panic and SIGABRT; in every profile it is UB.
mechanism.secondary_defect: B57-F2: OSSL_AA_DIST_POINT_TT was transcribed with offsets 16/20/24/28, omitting `dp_reasons` at 16, so the encoder/free walk bound the boolean fields one member low and left `containsSOAPublicKeyCerts` (offset 32) unbound. Reproduced as a wrong-decoded-value assertion while proving B57-F1; fixed by deriving every OSSL_AA_DIST_POINT offset with `core::mem::offset_of!`.

repair.abstraction: src/asn1/utl.rs: `is_inline_boolean(&Asn1Item)` (itype PRIMITIVE and utype BOOLEAN), `read_inline_boolean(*const c_void) -> c_int` and `write_inline_boolean(*mut c_void, c_int)`, the last two via `ptr::read_unaligned`/`ptr::write_unaligned` at c_int width.
sites: src/asn1/fre.rs:231 (item_embed_free): the non-primitive null guard no longer reads the slot; src/asn1/fre.rs:129 (primitive_free) skips the pointer read for `is_inline_boolean`; src/asn1/fre.rs:166 writes the BOOLEAN default through `write_inline_boolean`.
src/asn1/i2d.rs:237 (item_ex_i2d): the non-primitive null guard no longer reads the slot; src/asn1/i2d.rs:629 reads the boolean through `read_inline_boolean`.
src/asn1/tasn_prn.rs:223 (asn1_item_print_ctx): an inline boolean is treated as present without a pointer read.
src/asn1/new.rs:552/645 and src/asn1/d2i.rs:1061 write the boolean through `write_inline_boolean`.
repair.width_and_alignment: four-byte c_int at the field's real offset; `read_unaligned`/`write_unaligned` make the alignment assumption explicit and sound even though the current offsets are 4-aligned.
repair.abi: No `#[repr(C)]` layout, size, offset, exported symbol, signature or lint attribute changed.
